items.item_text: Bachelor’s Degree in Biological Sciences or related field and/or equivalent combination of education and experience.
Prior hands-on experience working with laboratory rodents in a research setting, including handling and basic procedures.
Prior experience working in a research laboratory environment involving both in vivo and molecular techniques
2 years related laboratory research experience or training
Hands-on experience with molecular biology techniques (including qPCR, Western blot, and/or immunohistochemistry).
Prior experience with rodent models and in vivo experimental procedures.
Experience assisting with surgical procedures and/or behavioral assays in rodent models.

The Department of Medicine is seeking a Staff Research Associate I to join an innovative neurogastroenterology research program focused on advancing the understanding of gastrointestinal and neurological disease. In this hands-on laboratory role, you will support ongoing in vivo rodent studies and molecular research by performing rodent handling, tissue collection, and a variety of molecular techniques, including qPCR, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. You will also assist with data organization, experimental documentation, and day-to-day laboratory operations. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, eager to develop technical expertise, and capable of working with increasing independence after onboarding while contributing to the successful execution of high-quality research and established experimental protocols.

the final candidate who accepts an offer of employment will be required to disclose if they have been subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct; or have filed an appeal of a finding of substantiated misconduct with a previous employer.
Ability to use a personal computer and standard software applications.
Required Ability to prioritize tasks and manage multiple responsibilities, including maintaining complete, accurate, and well-organized records.
Ability to follow detailed scientific protocols with precision and work effectively in a team environment.
Strong attention to detail and ability to perform repetitive tasks accurately.
Good oral and written communication skills in English.
Demonstrated ability to execute experimental procedures independently after initial training, with strong reliability and attention to detail.
Strong organizational and time management skills.
